title: refactor: colocate repository maintenance tooling
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves repository maintenance scripts beside the systems they maintain: username synchronization into `enter.pollinations.ai`, Polli embeddings into `apps/polli`, and GitHub project automation into `operations/github`.
- Colocates the project-manager prompt and operational documentation with their consumers, fixes prompt resolution, and removes the stale GitHub automation overview.
- Updates the minimal GitHub workflows and Tinybird source reference to use the new paths, while simplifying CI test discovery.
- Leaves `.github` focused on issue templates and workflow entrypoints; runtime behavior is otherwise unchanged.

Validation:
- 15 Node tests pass.
- Python modules compile and the relocated prompt loads successfully.
- Changed workflows parse as valid YAML.
- `git diff --check` passes.

gist.headline: Tools found their gardens
gist.blurb: The maintenance tools have moved closer to the systems they tend. Less wandering through `.github`, more sensible little tool sheds.
gist.summary: Repository maintenance tooling was relocated beside its consumers: username sync scripts now live in `enter.pollinations.ai`, Polli embedding code in `apps/polli`, and GitHub project automation in `operations/github`, with workflow paths and prompt resolution updated accordingly.
gist.impact: Contributors get clearer ownership and more reliable local tooling paths while GitHub workflow entrypoints remain lean and runtime behavior stays the same.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden shed organization scene: Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, carries labeled maintenance tools to nearby garden plots representing `enter`, `apps/polli`, and `operations/github`. Small code-plants grow beside each plot while a CRT monitor robot happily files workflow scrolls into a compact `.github` mailbox.
